candidate_review.reason: The broad direct sites are one/few argument or output conversions per process. They are permitted host ABI boundaries and absent as a shared material normal-binary owner.
The exact helpers are broad, but prior telemetry-free profiles show nil checks or zero-flat parents with unlike descendants; this route is explicitly closed.
Direct reach is concentrated in concurrency workloads. Current normal profiles already close call/member/index lowering with no new exact shared leaf.
Counts mix scheduler handles/capacity and explicit host conversions. Shape telemetry separates those reasons; normal profiles place the material service conversion helpers below one percent.
Each exact interface recovery repeats only across related scheduler/mutex applications and is required by the runtime-service ABI.
No exact callable runtime conversion reaches three unlike applications. The only repeated exact shape reaches two related mutex rows.
The exact shapes repeat only inside primitive-math, nominal-numeric, or regex families and encode semantic error payloads on cold/error paths.

decision.reason: No exact safely removable boundary is both material and present in three unlike direct-main applications. Broad sites are explicit host ABI, previously closed control/call routes, required runtime services, native Go union/interface lowering, or identity-bearing nominal allocation.

heap_nominal_review.reason: Concrete heap literals have distinct mutable identity, escape, return, storage, and interface lifetimes. Copy/value substitution is not semantics-preserving, and nominal-name rules are forbidden.
